title: Integrate backend processing for PDF and image tools (upload → process → download)

requirements.text:
Implement backend tool-processing endpoints in the single Motoko actor to support real file conversion/compression workflows for the existing tools:
- PDF to Word (PDF in → DOCX out)
- Image Compressor (image in → compressed image out)
- Image Resize & Compress (image in + resize/format/quality options → processed image out)
The backend must accept file bytes, perform the requested operation by calling a real external API over HTTPS (or another real, non-placeholder processing implementation), and return processed bytes plus output filename and contentType.

quotes:
Convert all tool pages into real working tools by adding backend integration:
- Use APIs or serverless functions
- For PDF tools use real PDF conversion API
- For Image tools use real compression/resize API
Ensure upload → process → download works correctly.

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes callable methods for each supported operation (PDF→DOCX, image compress, image resize+compress) and returns: processed bytes (Uint8Array/Blob), output filename, and content type.
Backend rejects unsupported input types (e.g., non-PDF for PDF→DOCX) with clear errors.
Backend errors are propagated as structured errors that the frontend can normalize via existing error handling.
All backend logic remains in backend/main.mo (single-actor architecture).

requirements.text:
Add a backend job/operation model that allows the frontend to show upload/progress states and reliably download outputs, while staying compatible with large files. Support at minimum:
- An operation identifier (e.g., tool id + parameters)
- Upload initiation and incremental upload (chunking) if needed
- A processing step that runs after upload finalization
- A retrieval step that returns the processed bytes + metadata
Use the existing blob storage mixin already included in backend/main.mo where appropriate to store uploaded/processed blobs during the workflow.

quotes: Ensure upload → process → download works correctly.

acceptanceCriteria: Frontend can upload a file, trigger processing, and then download the resulting file without relying on any client-side placeholder processing.
Intermediate and final artifacts are cleaned up after completion/failure (or have a clear retention policy), preventing unbounded storage growth.
The backend API supports reporting coarse progress states (e.g., uploading/processing/ready) sufficient for the current UI progress components to display meaningful status.

requirements.text:
Replace the placeholder mutation in frontend/src/hooks/useQueries.ts so it calls the backend for real processing instead of throwing "Backend processing not fully implemented". The hook must support:
- Selecting the operation (at least: pdf-to-word, image-compressor, image-resize-compress)
- Passing operation parameters (for resize/compress: targetWidth, targetHeight, maintainAspectRatio, format, quality)
- Upload progress callback compatible with the existing tool pages’ progress UI
- Returning processedBytes, filename, and contentType

quotes: Convert all tool pages into real working tools by adding backend integration... Ensure upload → process → download works correctly.

acceptanceCriteria: useProcessFile no longer throws the placeholder error and instead performs a real backend call sequence.
Upload progress updates the existing progress UI in tool pages that use a Progress component (e.g., PDF→Word, Image Compressor).
On success, the hook returns processedBytes + filename + contentType that can be downloaded via existing download helpers.

requirements.text:
Update the tool pages to use backend-driven processing end-to-end (upload → process → download) and remove any client-side-only placeholder claims that contradict backend processing:
- frontend/src/pages/tools/PdfToWordOnlineFreePage.tsx must convert via backend and download a DOCX.
- frontend/src/pages/tools/ImageCompressorOnlineFreePage.tsx must compress via backend and download the processed image.
- frontend/src/pages/tools/ImageResizeCompressOnlineFreePage.tsx must resize/compress via backend using the page’s current settings (dimensions, format, quality, aspect lock).
Ensure the output filenames and content types are correct for downloads.

quotes: Convert all tool pages into real working tools by adding backend integration... For PDF tools use real PDF conversion API... For Image tools use real compression/resize API

acceptanceCriteria: PDF to Word: uploading a PDF and clicking convert results in a downloadable .docx file that opens in Word/Google Docs.
Image Compressor: uploading an image and clicking compress results in a downloadable processed image with the expected (compressed) size change in typical cases.
Image Resize & Compress: processing uses the selected width/height/format/quality settings and downloads the resulting file with the correct extension and content type.
Any privacy/security FAQ or note that currently states processing is "entirely in your browser" is updated to accurate English text consistent with backend processing.
Errors from the backend display in the existing Alert UI with a user-friendly message.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo; add backend/migration.mo only if persistent state schema changes require it.
Do not edit files in frontend immutablePaths (e.g., frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, frontend/src/components/ui/*).
No external databases or additional backend services; any integration must be performed from the single canister backend (e.g., via HTTPS outcalls) or via real in-canister processing.
nonGoals: Implementing third-party authentication beyond Internet Identity.
Adding new tool pages/routes beyond the existing tools registry and routes.
Real-time processing via WebSockets or push notifications.
Adding unrelated UI redesign or new marketing pages.
